topic.title: One day on $25,000 a year vs one day on $25 million a year

title: Rohan makes $25,000 a year. Sharma makes $25M ⏰
description:
What does one ordinary Tuesday look like on $25,000 a year, and on $25 million?
One hour, one day, one week, one year: both incomes split by the clock, before tax, computed. Both incomes are round, illustrative numbers, not a real person; the spending figures are assumptions. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

lines.text: One Tuesday, two lives. Four clocks: an hour, a day, a week, a year.
Hour one, before tax. Rohan earns $12. I earn $12,019.
So his one hour beats my whole month of pay, $2,083.
Day one: $68,493. A brand-new sports car, every single morning.
Week one: $480,769. Enough for a house, paid in cash, by Friday.
Year one: $25 million. Rohan would need 1,000 years to earn that.
But the pay isn't the real gap. The real gap opens at midnight.
Midnight. My $68? Gone on rent, the bus and lunch. Bed.
My day cost $10,000, living large. Still $58,493 left, and it works the night shift.
Rohan's money sleeps when he sleeps. Mine never clocks out.
Alarm. Another Tuesday. And again, guess who earns what.
